comments.author: ru999gol
comments.story: Apple’s repair kill switch hasn’t been activated yet
comments.why: Shows a keyboard replacement being performed, revealing the labor involved
comments.text: Apple intentionally builds their keyboards in such a way that it is incredible difficult to replace, the amount of skilled labor required doesn't make it profitable to just replace the keyboard. Its eye opening seeing a keyboard replacement being performed: [VIDEO] Who is to blame for letting it get so far? I think its not just Apples fault, its governments fault not regulating them and consumers fault for still buying and even defending their practices (which you can very well observe in this thread).

comments.author: verisimilitude
comments.story: Apple Sued an iPhone Repair Shop Owner in Norway and Lost
comments.why: Failing MacBook keyboards and costly top case repairs
comments.text: His comments about the keyboard in the current MacBook Pros are particularly apt: [VIDEO] So, even a person holding 1 (2, 3!) genuine Apple keyboard(s) in their hands likely still couldn't do the repair -- they'd have to get a new top case. Out of warranty, I've heard it is a $500 repair. That seems to be a direct consequence of ignoring repairability (the maintainability ship sailed long ago).

comments.author: shabble
comments.story: Don’t buy the MacBook Pros even on sale, in my opinion
comments.why: Explains what a MacBook keyboard replacement involves
comments.text: If it's just a keycap (and maybe even the butterfly mechanism) that shouldn't be too bad. [VIDEO] (from about 5:20) talks a bit about what's involved in an actual keyboard replacement, if you ignore some of the histrionics. I think from what I've heard that for actual replacements, Apple will swap out the whole 'top case' subassembly, which could be a 4-500$ part if it's not covered under warranty.
